docs.title: Titan Share Price: Nomura, Motilal rate ‘Buy’ despite miss in Q2 jewellery segment growth
docs.text: Titan share price is under severe selling pressure after reporting 21% growth in the jewellery business in Q2FY27. This growth rate in the jewellery segment is below Nomura's expectations. However, watches, eyewear and international operations provide stronger support. Nomura has retained its ‘Buy’ rating while Motilal Oswal continues to include Titan among its preferred consumer discretionary holdings. The key pressure point is jewellery, where domestic sales, including CaratLane, grew 21% year-on-year, below Nomura's roughly 25% estimate. Within the core Tanishq, Mia and Zoya businesses, sales rose 20%, while CaratLane delivered a much stronger 32% increase. High gold prices, a later festive calendar and a high comparison base affected the jewellery numbers, but a stronger mix of studded jewellery and lower gold-coin sales could support margins. ALSO READJP Morgan’s festive picks: Why Titan, Lenskart, LG Electronics, Pidilite top the list The broader business was stronger. Consumer business sales, excluding bullion, digital gold and Titan Engineering and Automation Limited, grew 25% year-on-year. Watches grew 30%, domestic eyewear rose 28% and international sales increased 97%, including the contribution from Damas Jewellery. Jewellery growth missed expectations, but the mix is getting better Jewellery remains the centre of Titan Company's earnings story, accounting for 89.4% of sales and 89.7% of earnings before interest and taxes in FY26, according to Nomura's sales and earnings mix charts on page 3 of its report. The 21% growth in domestic jewellery sales was below Nomura's estimate of around 25%. Core jewellery sales at Tanishq, Mia and Zoya rose 20%, while CaratLane grew 32%, beating Nomura's 25% expectation. Gold prices were 46% higher year-on-year and broadly flat sequentially during the quarter. At the same time, buyer growth moderated to the mid-single digits from early double-digit growth in the first quarter. Gold-coin sales declined in the high-single digits, while the timing of Shradh and festive demand also affected the quarterly comparison. Nomura said, "However, studded jewelry growth has been much higher in the early thirties, aided by ‘Festive of Diamonds’ and brand-level promotions, while plain gold jewellery was up 20% y-y, and gold coin sales declined in the high-single-digits, indicating an improved mix and thus making a case for better margins in 2Q (vs guidance of 11%)." The shift towards studded jewellery is important because it can improve the overall product mix. Nomura expects that to give Titan Company some support on profitability even though the headline jewellery growth rate was below expectations. Titan Q2 update: Store expansion is picking up across key formats Titan Company also accelerated store additions during the quarter, particularly in jewellery. Tanishq, Mia and Zoya together opened around 29 stores during the second quarter, taking the total to 875. CaratLane added around 13 stores, taking its network to 396. That represents store growth of 12% for the core jewellery formats and 16% for CaratLane. ALSO READ5 investment themes, 20 stocks: How to ride India’s next capex boom Nomura had expected only 16 and five additions respectively. The stronger expansion is significant because CaratLane is increasingly positioned to capture demand for lower-caratage jewellery. Nomura said, "Store openings step up: TMZ/Caratlane opened around 29 /13 stores during 2Q, above our expectation of 16/5 stores, taking the total number of stores to 875/396, indicating store growth of 12%" The brokerage sees the expansion as part of Titan Company's effort to reach more consumers who are moving towards organised jewellery retailers and lower-caratage products. Watches and eyewear are giving Titan another growth engine The non-jewellery businesses delivered a much stronger quarter. Domestic watch sales grew 30% year-on-year, well above Nomura's 14% estimate. The analogue segment grew in the early thirties, helped by premiumisation, while smartwatches returned to high-single-digit growth after declining 23% in the year-ago period. Titan Company also added 34 watch stores during the quarter, taking its total network to 1,379 stores. Nomura had expected only 15 additions. Nomura said, "Sales growth of 30% y-y came in above our forecast of 14% y-y despite the festive quarter being in the base (2QFY26) vs in 3QFY27 this time." Domestic eyewear sales grew 28% year-on-year, compared with Nomura's estimate of around 15%. The brokerage attributed the performance to execution across strategic priorities, including a multi-brand approach, store upgrades and a sharper merchandise portfolio. The eyewear business did not add new stores during the quarter, but Titan Company continued upgrading its existing network. International operations are growing, while Damas is beginning to recover Titan Company's international business delivered 97% year-on-year sales growth during the quarter, although the comparison includes Damas Jewellery, which was consolidated from the fourth quarter of FY26. North America delivered double-digit growth, while the Gulf Cooperation Council region remained resilient and Tanishq showed an improvement in growth. The core Damas business remains under pressure, but management has indicated that early signs of recovery are emerging. Titan Company added one international store during the quarter, taking its international network to 164 stores. Nomura said, "Sales grew by 97% y-y (including Damas, which was consolidated w.e.f. 4QFY26), led by double-digit y-y growth in its North America business, while GCC held up with Tanishq reporting improvement in growth. The core Damas business remains impacted but management highlighted that it is seeing early signs of recovery." docs.title: AI boom behind 20% of US bond yield surge: What’s driving the rise?
docs.text: Bond yields continue to climb, and the AI boom is getting part of the blame. The 10-year US Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.34%, its highest since 2002, while the 30-year yield spiked to a 24-year high of 5.69%. First, a quick refresher. Bond yields move opposite to bond prices. So when investors sell bonds, prices fall and yields rise. A rise in yields also brings in the expectation of a higher-rate scenario. That is not good news. It is not looked upon favourably for the economy, corporates and borrowers. Why? Higher rates make loans costlier and squeeze growth. So what is behind the surge? The big question is, what is driving US yields higher: sticky inflation and possibly more Fed hikes, rising US fiscal burden, or something else? Industry experts blame a sell-off in US Treasury bonds, linked to AI. So how does AI come into the bond market story? The simple explanation is this. Capital is limited. AI companies are raising funds and offering higher rates to investors. For an investor, that changes the math. Holding US Treasury bonds is not attractive enough compared to holding AI debt. So money moves out of Treasuries and into AI paper. Treasury prices fall, and yields rise. That is one view. ING, Merrill and PIMCO's Christian Stracke each have an answer, and the answers differ. Here is how they stack up. ALSO READUS stocks face 20% valuation hit if Treasury yield reaches this key level: Fidelity Is AI Really Behind a Fifth of the Yield Jump? A recent note from ING strategists reports that inflation and fiscal deficits remain the biggest drivers of higher long-dated yields. AI accounts for about one-fifth of the recent rise, ING estimates. Much of the debate so far has focused on Big Tech's borrowing spree. It has forced companies to compete with governments for investor money. ING says that is only part of the story. ING does not rule out inflation as a reason behind rising yields. Separately, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh had highlighted the AI investment boom as a major source of price pressure during his testimony before the House Finance Committee. He noted the rapid development of data centers and the increasing demand for AI software and equipment as key aspects of the current US economy. ALSO READBlackRock sees AI-led earnings offsetting higher yields, stays bullish on US stocks Growth Hopes, Not Borrowing, Drive Most of AI's Push Where does AI's push come from, then? ING estimates that roughly 70% of AI's impact on long-dated yields comes from expectations that the technology will boost productivity and long-run economic growth. Only about 25% comes from higher AI-related corporate debt issuance. The logic is simple, according to ING. If AI makes businesses more productive, investors expect companies to borrow and invest more. That pushes up expectations for long-term interest rates. Those expectations can lift real bond yields even before productivity gains show up in economic data, the strategists wrote. In ING's view, a rise for productivity reasons reflects good news, not bad. Impact of AI on Bond Yields Source: ING Why Big Tech Bonds Are Crowding Out Treasuries Merrill's Chief Investment Office offers a different lens in its Capital Market Outlook. Its fixed income strategy team says the largest technology companies have issued nearly $280 billion of debt year-to-date to fund AI-related spending, citing Bloomberg data as of September 9. JPMorgan Chase estimated in June that $4.1 trillion in AI-related debt will be issued through 2030, reported CNBC. Many of these issuers carry high credit ratings and have been selling longer-maturity bonds. As a result, Merrill says, they are competing with long-dated Treasuries for the same pool of money. That pool includes insurance companies, pension funds, sovereign wealth funds and other investors focused on long-duration bonds. Merrill calls it a crowding-out effect among high-quality fixed income. The wider picture is similar. Merrill says investment-grade corporate issuance is running roughly 40% above last year and is on pace for a record, citing Bloomberg data as of September 8. Borrowing Adds to the Pressure The US government's worsening fiscal position is adding to the woes. Merrill says net interest expense has passed $1 trillion a year and now rivals total US defence spending. It adds that the Congressional Budget Office projects the fiscal 2026 shortfall to widen to roughly $2.1 trillion. So investors are being asked to absorb new supply from the Treasury and from corporate America at the same time, according to Merrill. The 30-year Treasury yield moved above 5.3% in August, a level not seen since 2007. Merrill says fiscal worries likely played a role. But it also says heavy supply, sticky inflation, reduced Fed demand and competition for investor capital were equally important. But is debt alone the answer? Merrill also notes that debt alone does not set interest rates. Between 2007 and 2020, US debt rose sharply even as the 10-year yield fell from roughly 5% to below 1%. Recent Treasury auctions, it adds, have drawn demand in line with historical norms. PIMCO's Stracke Goes Further: Is It All AI? PIMCO President Christian Stracke is also of the view that AI spending, not inflation, drove yields higher, according to a Bloomberg report. Stracke says capital demand from hyperscalers and the wider AI ecosystem is competing for a finite pool of capital. That, he argues, is lifting real rates and bond yields. The Verdict: Yes, But the Size Depends on Who You Ask So, is AI pushing yields higher? The short answer is yes, but the size of the push depends on who you ask. ING puts AI's share at about one-fifth of the recent rise, mostly driven by growth hopes rather than borrowing. Merrill sees AI-related debt as one part of a much bigger supply wave, alongside Treasury issuance. Stracke goes furthest, naming AI capital demand as the driver. docs.title: UBS sees 45% upside for this metal stock, says capex ramp-up not fully priced in
docs.text: Shyam Metalics and Energy is poised for significant growth in the coming quarters, mainly due to its new capital expenditure plans and increasing focus on value added products. Global brokerage UBS believes the company stands out in disciplined capital allocation, superior project execution, and efficient operations. UBS has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock and raised its target price by 24% to Rs 1,550. This implies an upside of a whopping 45% from the stock’s closing price of Rs 1,067.3 today, October 7. “Our review of completed and upcoming projects indicates that Shyam delivers capex at lower cost and with shorter timelines than the industry averages, supporting superior ROIC and faster growth,” UBS said. UBS on Shyam Metalics: Earnings improvement UBS expects the company’s earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) per tonne to improve to Rs 8,400 by FY31 from Rs 4,700 in FY26. This reflects a 24% growth on compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) basis over FY26 to FY31, compared to 12% CAGR growth between FY21 and FY26. ALSO READ3 Top Pharma CDMO Stocks in India to Add to Your Watchlist The brokerage believes the market has not fully priced in the capex ramp up and that consensus earnings upgrades will follow. UBS has raised its FY28 EBITDA guidance for the company by 3% and FY29 EBITDA guidance by 8%. “Shyam trades at 7.5x one-year forward EV/EBITDA, in line with the three-year average, leaving room for multiple expansion,” it added. “Shyam's earnings profile is changing as it moves from low-value intermediates to higher realisation products. We expect the contribution from intermediates to decline from 33% of revenue in FY26 to 12% by FY31E, with stainless steel increasing from 7% to 25% and finished steel from 44% to 52%,” the brokerage said. UBS added that this shift will be driven by new businesses such as hot rolled coil, cold rolling mills, special bar quality, stainless steel flat products, and railway wagons. The brokerage expects Shyam Metalics EBITDA growth to materially outpace volume growth as more and more revenue comes from downstream and value-added products. UBS on Shyam Metalics: Capex-led growth UBS believes the company’s growth is supported by a “large but focused” capital expenditure pipeline. The company is adding 1.58 million tonne per annum (MTPA) of hot rolled coil capacity, 0.8 MTPA of special bar quality, 4,800 railway wagons, 1.33 MTPA of stainless steel, and more aluminium foil and flat rolled capacity. ALSO READNuvama initiates coverage on RR Kabel with ‘Buy’: Sees 20% upside on export surge “Most of the capex is focussed on downstream businesses, which should support both revenue growth and margin expansion. Importantly, Shyam has demonstrated superior execution vs. industry peers. For major projects, Shyam's capex costs are 10-20% lower while completion timelines are 24-30 months vs. the industry norm of 30-36 months,” UBS said. UBS on Shyam Metalics: Next leg of growth UBS has raised its target price on Shyam Metalics as it believes the company will drive future growth from capex plans and value added products. The brokerage says the market has not fully priced in these factors and projects a 45% upside. docs.title: Sensex target 89,000 by June 2027: Why Morgan Stanley sees 24% upside led by 10 stocks
docs.text: Morgan Stanley expects the Sensex to reach 89,000 by June 2027, implying 24% upside from current levels, as it sees India’s earnings cycle gaining strength and the recent market weakness as more cyclical than structural. The brokerage is positioning for stronger domestic consumption, a pickup in private capital expenditure and improving financial-sector earnings, while remaining cautious on energy, healthcare and materials. In its India Equity Strategy Playbook, Morgan Stanley said the growth cycle is gaining traction, with domestic activity expected to improve even as global growth remains an important variable for Indian equities. The brokerage expects the investment-to-GDP ratio to rise to 37.5% over the next five years, pointing to a broader investment cycle supporting the economy. Morgan Stanley said, “The growth cycle is gaining traction: The principal catalyst is how the market gauges the growth gap between India and the world. That view may shift if global sentiment turns cautious on AI capex and/or India's growth accelerates.” ALSO READCipla to Torrent: JPMorgan’s 4 pharma picks with up to 25% upside potential Sensex target of 89,000 rests on a stronger earnings cycle Morgan Stanley's base case puts the June 2027 Sensex target at 89,000, with a 50% probability. At that level, the index would trade at a trailing price-to-earnings multiple of 23.5 times, compared with its 25-year average of 22 times. The brokerage expects Sensex earnings to compound at 16% annually through FY29 under this base case. Its assumptions include continued macroeconomic stability, higher private investment, robust domestic growth, steady global growth and lower oil prices from current levels. ALSO READ5 investment themes, 20 stocks: How to ride India’s next capex boom Morgan Stanley said, “Our BSE Sensex target of 89,000 implies upside potential of 24% through June 2027. This level suggests that the Sensex would command a trailing P/E multiple of 23.5x, ahead of the 25-year average of 22x.” The brokerage has also laid out a wider range of outcomes. Its bull case, carrying a 25% probability, puts the Sensex at 100,000 if oil prices fall below $75 a barrel and reflation policies succeed in lifting growth. Its bear case, also assigned a 25% probability, places the index at 66,000. That range makes oil prices, domestic policy and the pace of earnings growth key variables for the market over the next several quarters. Morgan Stanley sees the market weakness as cyclical The brokerage does not view the recent valuation pressure as evidence of a lasting deterioration in India's long-term growth prospects. It argues that concerns around demographics and artificial intelligence's impact on India's services economy are being overstated. Morgan Stanley expects slower fertility growth to have a limited near-term impact on the economy, while artificial intelligence could eventually raise labour productivity from a relatively low base. It also sees scope for India to increase its share of global goods trade as supply chains become more diversified. Morgan Stanley noted, “We therefore read the de-rating as cyclical - the outcome of a sharp negative gap in relative growth: India’s growth looks to have bottomed and is now trending higher, yet still trails that seen elsewhere, particularly in the US.” The brokerage also points to strong domestic equity flows, a developing initial public offering pipeline and weak foreign positioning as part of the current backdrop. Morgan Stanley added, “India is a defensive growth market: We see a major earnings cycle unfolding over the coming quarters that could take profit to GDP to new highs. For equity investors, the mix is compelling: broad-based growth, robust domestic equity flows, a nascent IPO pipeline, the weak trailing 12M relative performance, relative valuations just off all-time lows and foreign positioning that remains very weak.” At the same time, the brokerage sees risks from excessive new issuance, supply-side inflation pressures, prolonged high oil prices and a global shock. Domestic cyclicals, consumer discretionary and industrials get the biggest bets Morgan Stanley has built its sector portfolio around areas that can benefit directly from stronger domestic demand and capital spending. It has raised its allocation to consumer discretionary and industrials by 300 basis points each, while financials carry a 200-basis-point overweight. The brokerage expects lower interest rates and stronger income growth to support consumption, while higher private capital expenditure should benefit industrial companies. Morgan Stanley said, “Consumer Discretionary (+300bp): We expect a strong consumption growth helped by modest interest rates and robust income growth.” Industrials are another major preference, with Morgan Stanley expecting fresh capital spending across areas including defence, fertilisers, semiconductors and data centres. Morgan Stanley added, “Industrials (+300bp): A pickup in private capex drives our overweight. Energy, mining, defence, fertilizers, semi-conductors and data centres are the likely new capex drivers for India.” Financials also carry a sizeable overweight. The brokerage expects net interest margins to bottom out alongside stronger credit growth and benign credit costs. Morgan Stanley noted, “Financials (+200bp): NIMs are troughing. docs.title: Beyond warships: 2 stocks riding India’s Rs 69,725 cr small-shipbuilding push
docs.text: There is no denying that the investment opportunity around the naval defence build up gets almost all the attention. But perhaps, there is an alternate maritime capex opportunity that may be smaller than a destroyer and closer to the port - but exciting nevertheless. Tugs, workboats and pilot boats, all smaller boats in comparison, are directly tied to vessel handling, harbour operations, pilotage and offshore support, making port traffic and shipbuilding capacity relevant demand indicators. India’s ports handled more than 1.59 billion tonnes of cargo in FY2024-25. Major ports alone handled 915.17 MT in FY26, registering 7.06% year-on-year growth and surpassing their 904 MT target. The policy backdrop has also changed materially. Under the Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy, 288 contracts covering 456 vessels worth ₹19,748 crore had received in-principle approval by March 2026, with tugs specifically included among the eligible vessel categories. The government has since approved a ₹69,725-crore shipbuilding package, including ₹24,736 crore for the Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme, ₹25,000 crore for the Maritime Development Fund and ₹19,989 crore for the Shipbuilding Development Scheme. The latter aims to expand India's shipbuilding capacity to 4.5 million gross tonnes annually. Against this backdrop, two listed names come into focus: Knowledge Marine & Engineering Works and Cochin Shipyard. #1 Knowledge Marine & Engineering Works: The Higher-Purity Harbour-Craft Bet Knowledge Marine & Engineering Works Limited (KMEW) operates across port ancillary crafts, shipbuilding and repair, and dredging. Its vessel business covers conventional tugs, hybrid tugs, Green Tug Transition Programme (GTTP) tugs, pilot boats, speed patrol boats, mooring boats, service boats and multi-utility workboats. Its shipbuilding activity includes construction of small and specialised marine crafts, while the company also undertakes repair and refit of marine vessels. Its broader port-services capabilities include hydrographic surveys, pilotage and patrolling. Q1 FY27 Shows Where The Earnings Are Actually Coming From KMEW delivered a sharp improvement in Q1 FY27, with consolidated revenue from operations rising to ₹115.41 crore, up 138.2% YoY and 70.7% QoQ. Consolidated profit after tax (PAT) rose to ₹62.75 crore from ₹11.08 crore in Q1 FY26 and ₹23.53 crore in Q4 FY26. However, the 54.4% Q1 PAT margin should not be treated as a sustainable run-rate. Management has indicated a more normal operating-margin range of 35-40%, with the quarter benefiting from unusually strong dredging execution. The biggest change was the business mix. Dredging and ancillary services generated ₹104.41 crore of segment revenue in Q1 FY27, up 286.9% YoY and 52.8% QoQ. Shipbuilding contributed ₹21.22 crore versus zero in Q1 FY26 and ₹11.26 crore in Q4 FY26, with earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) of ₹3.41 crore. This matters for the maritime-capex thesis because KMEW's current earnings are still being driven primarily by dredging rather than by the construction of tugs and workboats. The shipbuilding opportunity is therefore a forward-looking growth engine, not yet the dominant earnings contributor. Strong Order Book But Its Composition Matters More As per the August 2026 earnings call, KMEW had an order book of over ₹1,300 crore, of which dredging was ₹240 crore, charter and hire was ₹850 crore and shipbuilding was ₹240 crore. The company also had an additional ₹200-crore inter-company order book placed with Knowledge Shipyard for Green Tugs and patrol boats. The company had 10 accommodation boats, 10 work boats, four cutter-suction dredgers, two 60-tonne bollard-pull green tugs and 10 hybrid-electric passenger ferries under its broader ongoing project portfolio. Separately, it was building three tugs and two boats for captive use and about 42 vessels for third parties. The order-book mix therefore shows that the immediate earnings base remains broader than shipbuilding, even as vessel construction becomes an increasingly important future growth driver. Saphale Could Change The Earnings Mix KMEW is undertaking roughly ₹1,000 crore of capex over the next 1.5 years, with about ₹250 crore earmarked for green tugs and green vessels, ₹450 crore for dredging and the balance for shipyard and shipbuilding operations. Phase I of the Saphale shipyard is expected to become operational by the end of FY27, with capacity for 14 vessels annually in Phase I and 18 vessels after completion of all phases. This is arguably the most important structural change in KMEW's investment case. The company is moving from owning and chartering marine assets towards building a dedicated manufacturing platform that can support a larger shipbuilding order pipeline. Management has indicated that the yard is already being positioned for orders over the next two financial years. It is therefore important to track order intake, vessel values, yard utilisation and execution margins as the Saphale facility ramps up. ₹1,000 Crore Capex Makes Funding A Key Monitor Debt remains an important investor monitor. By March 2026, consolidated borrowings stood at about ₹222.1 crore against cash and cash equivalents of ₹73.6 crore, implying net borrowings of roughly ₹148.4 crore. The debt to equity is at 0.39x. FY26 operating cash flow was negative at ₹200.4 crore, largely reflecting substantial deployment into other financial assets, while investing cash outflow was ₹104.4 crore, including ₹119.1 crore of property, plant and equipment purchases. docs.title: SEBI introduces a credit risk-o-meter for debt securities
docs.text: Securities and exchange board of India (SEBI) introduced a credit risk-o-meter for debt securities on Wednesday aimed to assist investors in assessing credit risk through colour-coded visualization prior to investing. The disclosure of risk-o-meter will be applicable to all listed and proposed to be listed issuances of non-convertible securities (NCS), commercial papers (CPs), securitized debt instruments (SDIs), security receipts (SRs) and structured debt /market-linked debentures (MLDs), whether issued by way of public issue or private placement. ALSO READStocks to watch for October 8: Senco Gold, Jubilant FoodWorks, Fino Payments, and more The new risk-o-meter will have to be mandatorily included in offer document, abridged prospectus, private placement memorandum, all ads of issuer and online bond platform provider (OBPPs) and their web and mobile platforms. The regulator has asked the exchanges and depositories to put in place necessary systems and processes to implement the measure within the next 45 days. Further, the regulator also exempted issuers issuing debt securities or non-convertible redeemable preference shares on a private placement basis from the requirement of hiring a merchant banker. The regulator had proposed the same in its consultation paper in August 2026. The exemption will only be applicable if the issuer is registered or regulated by a financial sector regulator in India (like SEBI, RBI, IRDAI or PFRDA) or the issuer is listed in any segment on any of the recognized stock exchange for a period of at least one year with no pending fines or penalties. The issuer must also not have defaulted in the last three financial years and the current financial year on any payments due in respect to the securities like repayment, interest, dividend. The exemption will be applicable only for unsubordinated or senior debt securities rated AA- or above secured by a first or pari-passu charge on the identifiable assets of the issuer. For public issuers, however, the debt securities can be secured or unsecured. If a debt security has multiple ratings, the lowest rating will be considered for determining eligibility for exemption. The regulator also increased the maximum number of international securities identification numbers (ISINs) maturing in a financial year for issuance of debt securities on a private placement basis from 14 to 17 with further six ISINs available for issuance of capital gains tax debt securities by authorized issuers. A maximum of 12 of these 17 ISINs will be allowed for the issuance of plain vanilla secured and unsecured debt securities with an aggregate upper limit of Rs 15,000 crore across issuances. ALSO READUS 10-year Treasury yield hits 5.32%: What is driving the rise? For each additional issuance of Rs 3,000 crore, one additional ISIN may be permitted to mature in the same financial year. A maximum of five ISINs maturing per financial year shall be allowed for structured debt securities, market-linked debt securities, floating rate bonds (FRBs), zero coupon bonds (ZCBs), and debt capital instruments (Tier II bonds). For issuers with only structured/market linked debt securities/FRBs/ZCBs/debt capital instruments (Tier II bonds), the upper limit will be of 12 ISINs in a financial year. Government of India serviced or extra budgetary resources (EBR) bonds, ESG debt securities will be excluded from calculating the ISIN limits.

docs.title: 5 investment themes, 20 stocks: How to ride India’s next capex boom
docs.text: India’s investment landscape is expanding beyond traditional infrastructure such as roads, railways and defence into a much broader set of themes. The numbers give some sense of the scale. The FY27 Budget has allocated ₹12.2 lakh crore towards capital expenditure, while the defence allocation stands at ₹7.85 lakh crore. But government spending is only one part of the investment story. Private-sector investment is also moving into areas that were relatively small parts of India’s industrial landscape a few years ago. Companies are committing capital to semiconductors, power and transmission, data centres, nuclear energy, aerospace and electric vehicles. Government initiatives such as the Production Linked Incentive scheme have also encouraged companies to build capacity and invest in domestic manufacturing. As a result, the opportunity is becoming broader than government expenditure alone. Some of these themes are already visible in the market, while others are still taking shape. Against this backdrop, we look at five investment themes that could play an important role in shaping India’s next growth cycle, along with the stocks positioned around them. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now Theme #1: Power & Transmission, Renewable Energy, Energy Storage Systems India’s power requirement is changing rapidly. Manufacturing, data centres, railways, electric vehicles and urbanisation are all adding to electricity demand. In 2026, peak power demand reached a record 270.8 GW. The power sector added 52.5 GW of capacity in FY26, up from 34 GW in FY25. Renewables are becoming a larger part of this expansion. Of the capacity added in FY26, 39.7 GW came from renewable energy. As of July 31, 2026, India had crossed 300 GW of non-fossil fuel-based installed generation capacity, reaching 60% of its 2030 target of 500 GW. Non-fossil sources now account for around 54% of the country's total installed generation capacity. But adding generation capacity is only one part of the equation. The electricity also has to reach where it is needed. This is where a ₹1.6 lakh crore worth High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) opportunity is expected to play a central role. The opportunity extends beyond HVDC to the broader transmission sector. The National Electricity Plan (2023-2032) projects peak power demand of 458 GW by 2032. The plan outlines an estimated ₹9.15 lakh crore investment in the transmission system. The transmission network is expected to expand from around 5 lakh circuit km in January 2026 to 6.48 lakh circuit km by 2032. Over the same period, transformation capacity is expected to rise from 1,407 GVA to 2,345 GVA. To capture these opportunities, these three companies are expanding their transformer capacity by up to 400%. The government has already started expanding this ecosystem. The proposed ₹1.86 lakh crore Green Energy Corridor is one example of the investment required to connect new renewable capacity to the grid. The opportunity is also extending beyond the grid itself. India's renewable expansion is creating a need for large-scale energy storage, including battery energy storage and pumped-storage projects. Nuclear power could add another layer to this investment cycle. Taken together, these developments point to a broader power-infrastructure opportunity. For investors, the focus is therefore not just on power generators, but on the companies supplying the equipment and systems needed to build, connect and manage India's expanding electricity network. Here are some of the stocks we covered recently that could ride this opportunity: #1 Tata Power: Integrated play with presence across power generation, transmission and renewable energy. #2 CG Power: Supplies transformers and critical power equipment #3 Power Grid: Direct beneficiary of transmission network expansion #4 Hitachi Energy: Benefits from grid modernisation and electrification demand You can read our entire coverage here… ALSO READIndia’s Rs 16 lakh crore data centre supercycle: 2 stocks connecting & powering the boom Theme #2: Semiconductors & Electronics: Building a New Manufacturing Ecosystem India’s electronics manufacturing push is gradually creating a wider ecosystem, spanning semiconductors, electronic components, specialised materials and chemicals. The government has been supporting this shift through the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM). ISM 1.0 came with a ₹76,000 crore outlay at a time when India has virtually no domestic semiconductor manufacturing base. The programme helped build the foundation needed for semiconductor design, fabrication and assembly and testing capabilities in the country. The recently approved ISM 2.0 has taken the planned government support to around ₹1.27 lakh crore. The second phase focuses on developing semiconductor equipment and materials in India, building indigenous semiconductor intellectual property and strengthening domestic and global supply chains. These pharma stocks, chemical players and fluorochemical companies are diversifying into semiconductor chemicals. Apart from this, due to increasing demand for ultra-clean water, water companies are also getting big opportunities in the semiconductor space. In addition to these two players, this hidden Murugappa Group company is also cashing in on the chip push. India’s electronics manufacturing growth is adding another layer to this theme. Mobile phone production has expanded sharply by 33X to ₹6.3 lakh crore, driven by government incentives and the PLI scheme. Now, the government's ₹62,500 crore mobile manufacturing scheme is opening another chapter of growth for both companies. docs.title: CAMS, HDFC AMC over BSE, CDSL: Nuvama lists top 2 picks amid weak market
docs.text: Think of the stock market as a busy highway. Prices are like the cars zipping past, fast and at a furious pace. But someone runs the toll booths, the record rooms and the fund houses. These businesses earn money whether you win or lose. So what happens to them when the highway slows down? Nuvama has assessed four market-linked businesses - Computer Age Management Services (CAMS), HDFC Asset Management Company (HDFC AMC), Central Depository Services (India) (CDSL) and BSE. Which one could handle a weak market better? Let's take a look - Weak markets test asset managers, but SIP flows offer support For asset management companies (AMCs), the key concern is the impact of falling equity prices on assets under management (AUM). The Nifty 50 declined 5.2% in the Q2FY27, which could limit growth in quarterly average assets under management. However, there is another side to the equation. Systematic investment plan (SIP) flows have remained strong. According to the Nuvama report, monthly SIP flows stood at Rs 32,000 crore in July and Rs 32,300 crore in August 2026. Nuvama expects listed AMCs to report aggregate revenue growth of 10.8% year-on-year and 3.8% quarter-on-quarter. Cost control could also help keep margins stable. ALSO READ20%+ loan growth, half HDFC Bank’s valuation: 3 private banks to watch The brokerage said, “Commentary on total expense ratio changes, specialised investment funds, distributor payouts, new fund launches and inflows shall be keenly watched.” CAMS and HDFC AMC: Can steady inflows offset weak markets? CAMS and HDFC AMC appear better placed in Nuvama’s comparison from a valuation perspective. The brokerage house in its report added that both are trading at relatively lower valuations while continuing to deliver growth despite difficult market conditions. Nuvama estimates that CAMS and HDFC AMC could deliver sequential net operating profit after tax (NOPLAT) growth of 1.8% and 6.1%, respectively. For CAMS, which provides registrar and transfer agent services to mutual funds, revenue growth is expected to remain muted at 2.4% quarter-on-quarter. The brokerage expects yields to remain stable. CDSL gets a boost from the IPO market Nuvama expects strong IPO activity to support CDSL during Q2FY27. According to the brokerage report, primary-market fundraising reached around Rs 92,600 crore during the quarter, nearly 9.8 times the previous quarter. Demat account additions have also picked up. Around 2.5 million accounts were added per month on average in July and August, compared with 1.9 million in Q1FY27. CDSL added 2.7 million demat accounts in August alone, its highest monthly addition in FY27 so far. Nuvama said, “The major revenue driver this quarter would be IPO-led revenue.” BSE faces a different challenge BSE’s performance is more closely linked to trading activity and regulatory changes. The brokerage report noted that the index option average daily premium turnover (ADPTV) fell 23.9% quarter-on-quarter to Rs 22,500 crore during Q2FY27. Nuvama estimates BSE’s revenue could rise 34.1% year-on-year but decline 8.5% quarter-on-quarter. Adjusted profit after tax (APAT) is estimated to increase 37.8% year-on-year while falling 13.5% sequentially. The brokerage said, “BSE’s fate depends on CAS regulation outcome.” ALSO READJP Morgan’s festive picks: Why Titan, Lenskart, LG Electronics, Pidilite top the list CAMS Vs HDFC AMC Vs CDSL Vs BSE: Which stock is better placed? Nuvama believes the market weakness creates selective opportunities rather than a broad-based call across the four companies. Its preferred picks are CAMS and HDFC AMC. The brokerage said, “We reckon CAMS/HDFCAMC are trading at attractive valuations of FY28E PE of 26x/28x and FY28E EV/NOPLAT of 26x/30x while delivering NOPLAT growth of 1.8% QoQ in such market conditions.” For CDSL, strong IPO activity provides support, but valuation remains a consideration. BSE, meanwhile, faces greater uncertainty around trading volumes and regulatory changes. docs.title: A Rs 9,000 cr stock controls Rs 59,500 cr of Britannia. Another trades at 12x
docs.text: High ROCE, Low PE, Still Ignored? Value for money stocks are easy to find. But such stocks that also earn a high return on the money put into them are much rarer. ROCE, or return on capital employed, shows the profit a company makes on every Rs 100 of capital it uses. PE, or price-to-earnings, shows what the market pays for every rupee of profit. I ran a screen for profit-making companies with a high ROCE and a low PE this week. Two smallcap names stood out, and each hides in the shadow of a far more famous one. The first is the 163-year-old Wadia Group flagship that controls Britannia. The second is a Kolkata company whose clients have included cable makers such as KEI, Havells and Apar. Both earn a ROCE above 30%. Both trade at a PE much lower than their respective industry medians. A low PE rarely comes without a reason. The real question is whether that reason still holds. Let us dive in. #1 Bombay Burmah: The Rs 9,000 Crore Stock Sitting on Rs 59,500 Crore of Britannia Incorporated in 1863, The Bombay Burmah Trading Corporation began life trading teak in Burma and moved into tea estates in South India in 1913. It is the Wadia Group's flagship. With a market cap of Rs 8,966 cr, it runs tea and coffee estates and makes auto electric parts and dental products. It also holds the group's crown jewel: majority control of Britannia Industries, the maker of Good Day and Marie Gold biscuits. The Britannia Maths the Market Keeps Ignoring Britannia's shareholding filing for the June 2026 quarter shows its promoter group holding 50.55% of the company. Almost all of that block sits with step-down subsidiaries of Bombay Burmah. At Britannia's market value of about Rs 1,15,858 cr, that stake is worth over Rs 59,000 cr on paper. Bombay Burmah's own market value is about 15% of that figure. Put simply, each Bombay Burmah share carries close to Rs 8,500 worth of Britannia stock, and trades at about Rs 1,300. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now There are reasons for the gap. The stake is not for sale, so shareholders only see its value through dividends passed up the chain. That is why Indian holding companies almost always trade at a discount. The group also carries the scar of Go First, the airline in which Bombay Burmah held about a third. When the airline collapsed in 2023, the company made provisions of Rs 1,866 cr, and FY23 ended in a consolidated loss of Rs 534 cr. Half the Profit Belongs to Britannia's Other Shareholders Financial YearFY21FY22FY23FY24FY25FY265-Yr CAGRSales (Rs Cr)13,39614,50716,62317,10918,29819,5398%EBITDA (Rs Cr)2,1501,5951,7262,8673,1363,43210%Net Profit (Rs Cr)1,278809-5341,6892,1992,49914% Source: Screener.in (Consolidated) EBITDA is operating profit before other income. Net profit includes the share of minority shareholders. Read the net profit row with care. It includes the part of Britannia's profit that belongs to Britannia's other shareholders, which is close to half. In the June 2026 quarter, consolidated profit was Rs 582.67 cr. Profit belonging to Bombay Burmah's own shareholders was Rs 288.16 cr, up about 20% on the year, as per results filed with BSE. On that owners' measure, earnings per share rose from Rs 52.96 in FY21 to Rs 178.10 in FY26, a compound rate of about 27%. The balance sheet has cleaned up too. Borrowings fell from Rs 6,542 cr in FY23 to Rs 1,590 cr in FY26. ROCE stands at 33%, with a return on equity (ROE) of about 19%. The Rs 249 Crore Block Deal On 18th September 2026, 18.34 lakh shares, or 2.62% of the company, changed hands in a block deal at about Rs 1,360 apiece. The stock jumped nearly 10% as traders guessed at a big new buyer. Filings with BSE a few days later told a quieter story. The seller was Nusli Wadia, whose stake fell from 10% to 7.37%. The buyer was Nowrosjee Wadia and Sons, a promoter group company, which now holds 44.57%. It was an inter-se transfer, shares moving from one family pocket to another. The promoter group's total holding stayed at about 74%. By 6th October, the stock had slipped to a fresh 52-week low. ALSO READ5 investment themes, 20 stocks: How to ride India’s next capex boom Valuation: 7x Earnings, and Flat for Five Years The share price of Bombay Burmah was around Rs 1,152 in October 2021 and as on 7th October 2026 it was Rs 1,285. That is a small gain in five years, and the stock is trading about 40% below its 52-week high of Rs 2,135. docs.title: Jio IPO countdown: Motilal sees Rs 11 lk cr valuation; may trigger Airtel & RIL re-rating
docs.text: India's biggest telecom listing is close. Jio Platforms (JPL) is preparing its initial public offering (IPO), the first time it will sell shares to the public. What price tag will it carry? And what does it mean for Bharti Airtel- its closest listed competition and the parent firm, Reliance Industries (RIL)? As per the Motilal Oswal report, Bloomberg has reported that Jio Platforms is seeking an equity valuation of around Rs 11 lakh crore ($114 billion) for its impending initial public offering (IPO). Motilal Oswal says this is broadly in line with its own valuation of Rs 11.2 lakh crore. But the IPO is not just about Jio. Its listing could have a wider impact on Bharti Airtel and Reliance Industries. So, what should investors watch? Jio Platform IPO valuation will set the tone The domestic brokerage house Motilal Oswal in its report noted that the proposed valuation of Rs 11 lakh crore translates into nearly 12 times FY28 estimated enterprise value to earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EV/EBITDA). That is around a 17% premium to the implied valuation multiple of Bharti Airtel’s India business, excluding its holdings in Indus Towers, Airtel Africa and Hexacom. “JPL IPO at Rs 11 trillion can potentially act as re-rating catalyst for Bharti,” the report noted. ALSO READLead Managers’ earnings surge to Rs 2,290 cr in 2026: How Q3 IPO rush drove 31% fee jump The brokerage believes Bharti deserves a similar valuation multiple because of its stronger free cash flow generation and higher return on capital employed. What happens to Reliance after Jio listing The Jio IPO could also change how investors value RIL. The company currently owns around 66.4% of JPL. After the listing, investors could apply a holding-company discount to this stake. However, Motilal Oswal believes the current RIL share price is already factoring in an 18–36% discount. There is another angle. Once Jio becomes separately listed, investors will have a direct route to its digital business. Yet RIL will still have its retail, energy and other businesses. The brokerage expects potential earnings upgrades from refining and petrochemicals, along with a recovery in retail growth and profitability. Will the Jio IPO trigger tariff hikes? This could be one of the biggest triggers for telecom stocks. According to the brokerage report, the delay in tariff hikes has been a key factor. Bharti is down 15% year-to-date, while RIL is down 23%, compared with a 13% decline in the Nifty 50. Motilal Oswal expects a smartphone tariff hike of around 15% in December 2026. “The delay in implementing a tariff hike (vs. initial expectation of Dec’25) has been a key reason for the muted stock performance of Bharti (-15% YTD) and RIL (-23%) vs. Nifty-50 (-13%), in our view,” Motilal Oswal report said. Could Jio’s listing change telecom stock allocations? The arrival of another large listed telecom company could make investors rethink their sector allocations. But the brokerage believes concerns about Bharti losing significant institutional money to Jio are exaggerated. One reason is JPL’s expected initial free float of only around 3%. ALSO READSeptember IPO rush: 34 issues raise Rs 39,340 crore; Rs 4.48 lakh crore pipeline ahead At the same time, Bharti has exposure beyond its core wireless business, including Indus Towers, Airtel Africa, data centres and financial services. What happens to earnings after the Jio Platforms IPO? As per the brokerage report, the combination of a Jio listing and an expected Vodafone Idea fundraise could strengthen the case for a tariff increase. The brokerage report added, “After the JPL IPO and Vi’s impending fundraise, we believe the case for a tariff hike is stronger and build in a smartphone tariff hike of ~15% in Dec’26, which should provide visibility on delivering ~15% EBITDA CAGR over FY26-29E.” Motilal Oswal remains constructive on Bharti, Bharti Hexacom (BHL) and RIL, while retaining a Neutral view on Indus Towers, Tata Communications and Vodafone Idea. “We continue to prefer Bharti (improved FCF, deleveraging, continued premiumisation), BHL (pure-play exposure to high-growth wireless and HBB businesses, lower capital allocation risks vs. Bharti), and RIL (closer to bear case valuations, likely higher O2C earnings in the near term),” the brokerage report added. docs.title: Jefferies top NBFC bets for Q2: Bajaj Finance, Chola & Shriram set for robust earnings
docs.text: The September quarter could bring another strong earnings season for non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). Loan growth has remained healthy, asset quality has stayed largely stable and credit costs are showing signs of moderation. Funding costs have started moving higher, while the weak monsoon could become a concern for rural borrowers. According to the Jefferies report dated Oct, 2026, profit after tax (PAT) for its covered NBFCs could rise 34% year-on-year (YoY) in the September quarter, excluding Piramal Enterprises and IIFL Finance. The brokerage expects loan growth of around 21%, supported by lower credit costs. Which NBFCs could stand out? Let's take a look - Jefferies on NBFCs: Strong loan growth sets the tone The September quarter typically brings some seasonal weakness. Yet disbursements have remained healthy, according to Jefferies' channel checks. Vehicle demand has also stayed firm. Auto registrations during the quarter rose 36% YoY for trucks, 28% for passenger vehicles and 14% for tractors. Jefferies in its report on Oct 6, 2026 expects aggregate assets under management (AUM), excluding Piramal and IIFL Finance, to grow 21% YoY, compared with 20% in the June quarter. “Strong profit growth: For Sep Q, we expect covered NBFC's profit to grow 34% YoY (ex-Piramal/ IIFL), led by 21% loan growth and lower credit costs,” added the report. ALSO READ3 Top Pharma CDMO Stocks in India to Add to Your Watchlist Gold financiers are expected to lead AUM growth at 44%, while diversified NBFCs could grow 25%. Affordable housing finance companies (AHFCs) are expected to grow 21%, while auto NBFCs could see 17% growth. Jefferies on NBFCs: Funding costs are the next test Yields on AAA-rated NBFC bonds have risen 54 basis points since June-end, while marginal cost of funds has increased by around 15–20 basis points. This could put pressure on net interest margins (NIMs), which measure the difference between what lenders earn on loans and what they pay for funds. In the report dated Oct 6, Jefferies expects some divergence. NIMs could improve at Shriram Finance, Poonawalla Fincorp and Piramal Enterprises, while Bajaj Finance and Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company could see a 5–10 basis-point decline. Jefferies on NBFCs: Asset quality remains the key watchpoint The Jefferies' channel checks suggest collections have remained steady despite seasonal weakness. Tighter underwriting, particularly for unsecured loans, has also helped keep delinquencies under control. CreditAccess Grameen's loans overdue by more than one day fell 10 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 2.1%. Mahindra Finance also reported stable Stage 3 assets. The report noted, “Weak monsoon this year (-13% deficit) could impact rural demand and asset quality; mgmt commentary in this regard will be the key.” Why Jefferies likes four NBFC stocks Jefferies remains positive on the NBFC sector. The global investment bank believes valuations, at around 2.2 times forward one-year book value, are close to trough levels. Its preferred names are Bajaj Finance, Aditya Birla Capital, Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company, and Shriram Finance. At Bajaj Finance, the brokerage expects around 28% YoY profit growth. Aditya Birla Capital, meanwhile, could benefit from healthy growth and a potentially favourable impact from higher rates. ALSO READNuvama initiates coverage on RR Kabel with ‘Buy’: Sees 20% upside on export surge For Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company, broad-based growth and lower credit costs are expected to support earnings. Jefferies expects around 30% profit growth. Shriram Finance could benefit from a possible pickup in growth during the second half of the financial year and lower funding costs. docs.title: Stocks to watch on Oct 7: Titan, Mphasis, JSW Cement, banks in focus ahead of RBI policy
docs.text: Every trading day starts with the same quiet question - what will everyone be talking about by 9:15 AM? For October 7, the answer might be a jeweller, a tech firm, a cement maker and an entire banking sector and rate sensitives - all waiting for one announcement. Before looking at the outlook for October 7, a quick look at how markets fared on October 6. The Sensex closed at 73,067.81, up 685.34 points (0.95%), and the Nifty finished at 22,776.10, gaining 220.35 points (0.98%). The Nifty even picked up another 58 points during the closing auction session. Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments said, "Crude oil prices slipped below the $100 mark after a large G7 stockpile release and alternative supply measures helped offset disruptions to vessel movements through the Strait of Hormuz." ALSO READFrom 7.1% to 15.3%: HDFC Bank’s loan growth comeback is hard to ignore He added that this, along with strong Q2 updates from financials and retail, "improved investors' sentiment and supported a rebound from the oversold levels." Here is a look at the stocks that are likely to remain in focus on October 7 trading session - Titan The Q2FY27 earnings season has begun, while companies are also announcing their Q2 business updates. Titan reported 25% year-on-year growth across its consumer businesses in Q2 FY27. The company added 78 net new stores in the quarter, taking the network to 3,758 stores. Domestic business grew 22%, while international surged 97%. In theJewellery segment, around 21% growth, with 42 new stores bringing the total to 1,269. Furthermore, Tanishq, Mia, Zoya and beYon grew 20% together, while CaratLane stood out at 32% with 13 new stores. Mphasis Mphasis announced an agreement worth about £35.4 million with Social Security Scotland. The company will manage and maintain the platform that handles benefit applications, eligibility decisions and payments for around 2 million citizens. JSW Cement JSW Cement commissioned an additional 1 MTPA grinding unit in Nagaur, Rajasthan. This lifts the plant's capacity to 3.50 MTPA and the company's total grinding capacity to 25.1 MTPA, with clinker capacity standing at 9.74 MTPA including its joint venture. ALSO READJP Morgan’s festive picks: Why Titan, Lenskart, LG Electronics, Pidilite top the list The Big Event: RBI MPC The RBI Monetary Policy Committee's decision is due on October 7, which makes it the main reason traders will be glued to their screens. The stocks and sectors in focus include - Banks: ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank Insurers: ICICI Lombard, SBI Life and HDFC Life Rate-sensitive sectors: Real estate, automobiles and leveraged NBFCs The brokerage house Emkay in its report added, "We expect the RBI to kick off the rate hike cycle with a cautious 25bp increase, while retaining a neutral stance and signaling a higher-for-longer rate environment; a 50bp hike remains an outside risk as tighter global financial conditions increasingly shape the RBI's reaction function. Inflation is emerging as the key concern, with pressures broadening beyond food and our 2HFY27 forecasts running ~20bps above the RBI's projections." Meanwhile, FCNR-led excess liquidity continues to keep monetary conditions accommodative despite a tactical mix of sterilization tools, making liquidity management an ongoing challenge. The October policy should offer greater clarity on the RBI's sterilization strategy, with a further OMO sales announcement possible," said Emkay in its report. docs.title: Deposit rate hike may lag due to ample liquidity
docs.text: The Reserve Bank of India’s 25-basis-point repo rate hike on Wednesday may take time to fully transmit to lending and deposit rates, as abundant liquidity leaves banks with little incentive to raise funding costs, experts said. “Transmission will likely be slower, except for loans directly linked to the external benchmark lending rate (EBLR), which must adjust faster. Given the surplus liquidity in the system, the weighted average call rate (WACR) remains relatively low, so transmission will remain muted until liquidity gets deployed or the RBI steps up its liquidity mop-up,” said Sachin Sachdeva, vice-president and co-group head, financial sector ratings, ICRA. ALSO READToday’s strength not tomorrow’s immunity: RBI governor Sachdeva said banks are also likely to take longer to raise deposit rates as they face little pressure to attract funds. “Deposit-side transmission is likely to begin only after a few months, once liquidity gets absorbed and lenders start chasing domestic deposits.” Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda, agreed that banks have little need to reprice deposits while they remain flush with liquidity. “Most lenders can meet short-term requirements via bulk deposits without committing to higher retail rates. Since deposit costs underpin the MCLR, lending rates cannot move up unless funding costs increase.” System liquidity surged to a record Rs 11.16 lakh crore on September 6, prompting the RBI to step up absorption through variable rate reverse repos (VRRRs), open market operations (OMOs) and forex swaps. The surplus has since moderated following RBI bond sales and tax-related outflows, but remained sizeable at Rs 4.98 lakh crore on October 6. The WACR, the operating target of monetary policy, ended at 5.37% on Wednesday, 13 basis points below the new repo rate of 5.50%, underscoring the drag that surplus liquidity could exert on monetary transmission. “A rate hike while maintaining a liquidity surplus creates counteracting forces that work against each other, so calibrated tightening was required. I expect liquidity to remain moderately in surplus till December. Deposit rates are likely to change only after December, depending on the liquidity conditions at that time,” said Alok Singh, treasury head at CSB Bank. The divergence between lending and deposit rates has already been visible. During July-August, banks’ weighted average lending rate (WALR) on fresh rupee loans hardened by 8 basis points, while the weighted average domestic term deposit rate (WADTDR) declined by 28 basis points, according to RBI data. ALSO READNBFCs account for half of new-to-credit originations: Report Going forward, the RBI will use an appropriate mix of liquidity-management tools and seek to align the WACR with the policy repo rate, Governor Sanjay Malhotra said in the Monetary Policy statement. At the post-policy press conference, Malhotra said he expects a large part of the surplus liquidity to be absorbed during the current financial year. “We believe that this higher liquidity is not a very long-term phenomenon because of natural reasons like currency leakage and reserve requirements of the banks, through our various operations, whether it is spot or sell-buy swap operations,” he said. “We have other tools like OMO, CRR and the spot intervention that we do to support the rupee,” Malhotra added.

docs.title: Cipla to Torrent: JPMorgan’s 4 pharma picks with up to 25% upside potential
docs.text: JP Morgan has four pharmaceutical and contract research, development and manufacturing organisation (CRDMO) stocks on its ‘Overweight’ list, with Torrent Pharma offering the highest potential upside among the four, followed by Cipla. Divi’s Laboratories and Anthem Biosciences are the brokerage’s preferred CRDMO names, though their return potential is more limited at current levels. The four stocks are Torrent Pharma, Cipla, Divi’s Laboratories and Anthem Biosciences. JP Morgan’s broader coverage also includes Zydus Lifesciences with a ‘Neutral’ rating and Dr Reddy’s Laboratories with an ‘Underweight’ call, making the distinction important when looking at the brokerage’s preferred names. Torrent Pharma leads the pharmaceutical picks Torrent Pharma is JP Morgan’s strongest pharmaceutical preference among the names covered, with an ‘Overweight’ rating and a target price of Rs 5,950. The stock offers 24.7% upside to the brokerage’s target. The investment case is being driven by the integration of JB Pharma, continued strength in the domestic chronic therapies business and a better outlook for the US franchise. JP Morgan expects Torrent’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation and adjusted profit after tax to grow sharply in the September quarter, helped by the acquisition and improving operating performance. “India to gain from US, as management expects growth of 16% YoY from acquisition of JB Pharma. JB Pharma’s growth to be driven by outperformance in the chronic segment. US to see marginal decline YoY due to pressure in generics but increase 12% QoQ to $480mn owing to ramp-up in Leqembi, Lunivect and broader strength in specialty.” The integration of JB Pharma is central to the story because it adds scale to Torrent’s India business and strengthens its exposure to chronic therapies. JP Morgan expects the acquired business to outperform in this segment, while Torrent’s US operations should benefit from specialty products and new launches. The brokerage also expects Torrent’s India business to remain a key support as the company integrates the acquired operations. ALSO READNifty valuations hit 4-year low: CLSA reveals 14 picks; banks lead, tech gets 1 spot “Key catalysts: New product launches, speciality ramp-up, integration of India operations, semaglutide ramp-up.” Torrent therefore combines several earnings drivers rather than depending on a single product or geography. The domestic business provides the base, JB Pharma adds incremental growth and the US business offers potential upside through specialty products. Cipla has a more balanced domestic-US growth story Cipla carries an ‘Overweight’ rating and a target price of Rs 1,600 from JP Morgan, implying 19.5% upside. The brokerage expects revenue, earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation and adjusted profit after tax to grow in the September quarter, supported by the India business and continued strength in respiratory products in the US. The domestic franchise is particularly important to the near-term earnings outlook. JP Morgan expects strong growth in respiratory, cardio-diabetes and pain therapies, while the US business is expected to benefit from its respiratory portfolio and new products. “US sees large base growth of 7% YoY, with US respiratory and new products expected to remain strong. India is expected to grow 12% YoY with strong growth in 2Q in India respiratory, cardio-diabetes and pain for Cipla.” The company also has several product-related catalysts that could support the earnings trajectory. JP Morgan is watching the ramp-up of gVentolin and gAdvaair, along with other respiratory and peptide opportunities. ALSO READ3 Top Pharma CDMO Stocks in India to Add to Your Watchlist “Key catalysts: gVentolin and gAdvaair ramp-up, Symbicort and other peptide approvals/launches, Indore plant classification, Lanreotide supply resumption, India outperformance.” That gives Cipla a relatively balanced setup. Its domestic business can cushion pressure in US generics, while new launches provide opportunities to improve growth from overseas operations. Divi’s Laboratories has a strong business but limited upside Divi’s Laboratories is JP Morgan’s preferred CRDMO name, carrying an ‘Overweight’ rating and a target price of Rs 9,100. At current levels, however, the stock trades 4.7% above the brokerage’s target, implying 4.7% downside. The near-term earnings picture remains supported by the company's custom synthesis and manufacturing business, although growth is expected to moderate from the exceptionally strong base of the previous year. JP Morgan expects the generic and contract manufacturing business to face different operating conditions, with pricing pressure weighing on generics while custom synthesis remains the more attractive part of the business. “GQ/CM to see slow growth of 6% YoY owing to continued pricing pressure in generics; custom synthesis growth to moderate to 15% YoY from ~45% YoY in 2QFY26 but steady growth in core custom synthesis business.” The longer-term opportunity rests on new projects, capacity additions and commercialisation of products already in the pipeline. This gives Divi’s a business profile that is less dependent on the conventional generic drug cycle. JP Morgan's catalysts include new projects, additional capital expenditure and the ramp-up of its Akola operations. “Key catalysts: commercialisation of core custom synthesis business, aided by 2027 volume uptake, new launches/projects/capex, ramp-up in Akola operations, new launches/order wins.” The relatively limited return potential at present levels does not change JP Morgan’s positive business view, but it does make Divi’s a different proposition from Torrent Pharma and Cipla in terms of the target-price opportunity. docs.title: Jet fuel, fares and demand: What could shape IndiGo’s earnings?
docs.text: Airfares in India are likely to stay high in the coming quarters, with the price of jet fuel emerging as the biggest unknown. IndiGo's passenger yields rose about 21% in the April to June quarter, while its fuel cost per available seat kilometre went up about 80%, according to a Nomura report. The airline has issued guidance for a 25% rise in passenger revenue per seat kilometre in the July to September quarter. Singapore jet fuel, the benchmark for international purchases, was at $164.50 a barrel on September 30, against $93.36 on February 27 before the war in the Middle East began, as per the report. ALSO READKalyan Jewellers Q2 revenue jumps 26%; India business grows 27% IndiGo fares rise on fuel costs Fuel charges took up 44% of IndiGo's revenue in the first quarter of FY27, up from about 30% before the war. Fuel also made up about half of the airline's costs, compared with about 40% earlier, according to Nomura. The airline's cost per seat kilometre, excluding foreign exchange and acquisition costs, rose 36% from a year earlier. Most of that increase came from fuel. Revenue per seat kilometre rose 19% in the same period. That meant IndiGo recovered roughly 53% of the cost increase through higher fares, as per the report. Nomura expected the recovery to settle between 50 and 70%, and to reach close to 70% in the second quarter. Domestic ATF prices and airfares The domestic picture was shaped by a government and oil marketing company cap on aviation turbine fuel. The cap limited the increase to 25% over the March base from April 1 to June 8, according to the report. Domestic rates moved to market-linked levels from June 9. International routes were at market rates throughout, which meant the relief was partial and temporary. Global airlines pass on fuel costs IndiGo's recovery was in line with global airlines, as per the report. United Airlines recovered about 50% of its fuel cost increase in its latest reported quarter. It guided for 80 to 90% recovery in the following quarter and a full recovery by the one after that. American Airlines also recovered about 50%, according to the report. ALSO READDomestic air traffic falls 6.3% in August; IndiGo, SpiceJet lose share Jet fuel prices and IndiGo margins Nomura's base case assumed some easing of the war in FY28, with jet fuel averaging $135 a barrel against about $155 in FY27. As a result, it expected fuel cost per seat kilometre to fall about 13%. Fares were not expected to fall by the same proportion. In FY24, fuel cost per seat kilometre fell 17%, and yields stayed flat, the report noted. On that basis, IndiGo's EBITDA margin was estimated to improve from about 15% in FY27 to between 20 and 23% in FY28 and FY29, according to the report. FY28 EBITDA was pegged at about Rs 240 billion in the base case. The International Energy Agency projected a global oil surplus of 4.6 million barrels a day by 2027, which could ease prices, as per the report. The sensitivity was sharper in both directions. Every 12 to 13% rise in jet fuel prices would cut FY28 EBITDA by 15 to 20%, depending on capacity growth, according to Nomura. A fall of similar size would raise it by a comparable margin. Higher airfares weigh on passenger demand Higher fares have started to coincide with weaker traffic. Total passenger traffic was down 5% in the first five months of the fiscal year, as per the report. Domestic traffic was flat, while international traffic fell 20%. Nomura still saw demand as resilient and expected only a moderate dip in load factors. It also expected IndiGo's capacity growth to be flat in the second quarter before picking up in the second half. Lower load factors from expensive tickets were listed among the risks, along with any cap on fares or ancillary revenue, according to the report. IndiGo’s domestic market share advantage IndiGo carried about 64% of domestic passengers at the end of FY26, while the Air India group had about 27%, as per the report. Nomura said Air India's older and mixed fleet, lower utilisation and premium focus left it with a higher cost base. Its long-haul widebody routes were expected to turn unprofitable first if fuel stayed high. Akasa Air had a thinner liquidity buffer, according to the report, as it funded fleet expansion and international entry together. IndiGo held cash of Rs 529 billion at the end of the June quarter. Nomura initiated coverage on InterGlobe Aviation with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 6,000. That implied about 20% upside from the Rs 4,984 closing price on September 30, as per the report.

docs.title: RBI rate hike: Shorter term debt funds turn attractive
docs.text: Debt fund managers are advising investors to favour short-to-medium duration funds after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised the repo rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday, arguing that bond markets have already priced in a large part of the expected tightening cycle. Fund managers expect another 50 bps of rate hikes over the next few months, but believe much of the adjustment in yields has already taken place. This, they said, has made the two-to-four-year segment particularly attractive, with yields of around 7.8-8% offering healthy accrual without taking excessive duration risk. ALSO READIndices fall as RBI hikes repo rate to tame inflation Deepak Agrawal, CIO–debt, Kotak Mahindra AMC, said the rate hike was in line with expectations given the rise in inflation. He expects another 50 bps of hikes in FY27, considering global dynamics and average inflation of around 5-5.1% in FY28. Agrawal recommended short-to-medium duration funds as the expected rate hikes are largely discounted in this segment. For investors with an investment horizon of 18 months or more, he also sees opportunities in long-duration funds, with yields on 30-40-year bonds reaching 7.9-8%. Anurag Mittal, president & head–fixed income, UTI AMC, echoed the view, saying the market has already priced in up to 100 bps of rate hikes and most of the adjustment in yields has taken place. He expects another 50-75 bps of hikes in the current cycle. Mittal recommended funds with a duration of two to four years, including short-term and corporate bond funds. Current yields of 7.8-8% in these segments are attractive without exposing investors to meaningful duration risk, he said. Basant Bafna, head–fixed income, Mirae Asset Mutual Fund, said Wednesday’s policy aligns the RBI with the global hawkish turn and represents an “insurance hike” aimed at reducing the need for more aggressive tightening later. He expects one more hike in December and a shallow tightening cycle, with developments in West Asia and the second-order impact of El Niño remaining key factors to watch. While the overall yield curve has steepened and is pricing in most of the negatives, Bafna said the six-to-18-month segment continues to offer attractive risk-adjusted returns. Vikas Garg, head–fixed income, Invesco Mutual Fund, expects the current growth-inflation dynamics to warrant another two to three rate hikes to anchor inflation expectations. However, he said the policy-rate trajectory could change rapidly depending on global developments. “Any resolution of the West Asia conflict could lead to a sharp correction in crude oil prices, thereby easing inflationary pressures,” Garg said. He recommended corporate bonds with maturities of one to three years, where yields of 7.75% and above remain attractive even after factoring in the expected rise in inflation. Corporate bond spreads over government securities are also significantly above their historical averages, providing an additional margin of safety, he said. ALSO READSensex target 89,000 by June 2027: Why Morgan Stanley sees 24% upside led by 10 stocks High-accrual strategies with moderate duration across ultra-short duration, low-duration and short-term bond funds could also offer an attractive risk-reward proposition, according to Garg. Edelweiss Mutual Fund, in a note, said it expects the repo rate to reach 6.25% by early 2027, with the yield curve likely to flatten as higher policy rates transmit to shorter-maturity bonds. It recommended AAA-rated bonds maturing in two to three years, with fund maturity aligned to investors’ intended holding periods. Following the rate hike, the benchmark 10-year government bond yield rose 5 bps to close at 7.24%, its highest level since December 2023.
